children: Oracle Corp. (ORCL, Financials), the cloud infrastructure and enterprise software company, rallied after management outlined a clearer path for funding its massive artificial intelligence buildout.
Oracle said capital spending should peak this fiscal year and next as it expands cloud capacity, while additional outside financing for the rest of the cycle should be limited to $20 billion.
That amount is expected to be split evenly between debt and equity.
The company also expects free cash flow to turn positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 and exceed $30 billion in fiscal 2029 as capital spending begins to fall.
The update addresses one of the biggest concerns hanging over Oracle: how much debt and stock issuance will be required to support AI infrastructure commitments.
As of Aug. 31, Oracle had about $125.34 billion in borrowings and $36.37 billion in cash.
Management expects to stop relying on outside funding for growth from fiscal 2029 and bring net debt below 3.5 times core earnings that year.
Oracle also forecast fiscal 2030 revenue above $225 billion and adjusted EPS above $21.
The next catalyst is whether Oracle can execute that financing plan without materially weakening margins or the balance sheet.

title: Oracle Jumps as AI Spending Plan Eases Financing Fears
